deckTitle: Trust & Betrayal — The 'Trust Me, Bro' Edition

cards.power: Both players reveal their hands. The one with the lowest value loses everything. If tied, you both lose.
cards.lore: We formed an alliance with the explicit intent of destroying each other. Why are you surprised?
cards.gradeReason: Betrayal as a mutual contract. Both players know. Both play anyway. Genius.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: two frogs shaking hands over a bomb timer. Mood: doomed solidarity.

jsonLegacy.power: Both players reveal their hands. The one with the weakest card must immediately copy the strongest move.
jsonLegacy.lore: We formed an alliance with the intention of betraying each other.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p2 TL

cards.power: Play only when an opponent leaves the room. Steal their best card.
cards.lore: Cowards live longer. It's simple biology.
cards.gradeReason: Three words. Zero ambiguity. The hyena knows exactly what it's doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: laughing hyena holding cards in front, dagger hidden behind. Mood: cheerful menace.

jsonLegacy.power: Conceal the dagger until the final moment.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p2 TR

cards.power: Cancel any "Promise" or "Alliance" made in the last 3 turns. Take 2 chips from the victim.
cards.lore: Words are wind. Contracts are paper. Paper burns.
cards.gradeReason: 'Words are wind. Paper burns.' That's not a card, that's a philosophy. Instant G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: rotund walrus setting a scroll on fire with a candle, looking smug. Mood: cheerful nihilism.

jsonLegacy.power: Words are wind. Contracts are paper. Paper burns.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p2 BL

cards.power: Look at an opponent's hand. Tell them you love them. Discard their highest card.
cards.lore: They were only pretending to like your mixtape to get the nuclear codes.
cards.gradeReason: The 'second dessert' lore is delightful but the mechanic needs a table to unlock it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: scheming cat in a monster costume eyeing a cake. Mood: domestic betrayal.

jsonLegacy.power: They were only pretending to be your monster to eat your second dessert.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p2 BR

cards.power: Check the bottom card of the deck. If it's a Trap, scream. Keep the card.
cards.lore: It's not paranoia if the universe is actually out to get you.
cards.gradeReason: Deck-check mechanic explains itself to death. The raccoon's trash-can energy is wasted on this rules text.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: raccoon peering over a trash can rim with binoculars, surrounded by conspiracy notes. Mood: justified anxiety.

jsonLegacy.power: Check the bottom card of the deck. If it's a Trap, someone nearby is planning...
jsonLegacy.lore: It's not paranoia if the universe is actually out to get you.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p3 TL

cards.power: Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Put them back in the worst possible order.
cards.lore: We hate them for lying. We pay them for the truth. We shoot them for receipt.
cards.gradeReason: Philosophical observation masquerading as a card. Tell me what to DO, not what to think.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: chameleon in a trench coat and tiny fedora studying a dossier. Mood: self-aware espionage.

jsonLegacy.power: We hate them for lying. We spy them for the truth.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p3 TR

cards.power: If a player steals from you, you may immediately steal two items from them.
cards.lore: I knew you'd turn on me, so I poisoned your coffee three weeks ago.
cards.gradeReason: Pre-emptive poison is a great concept but the card tells you what happened, not what to become.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: squirrel handing acorns to another squirrel, one marked with a tiny skull. Mood: cheery premeditation.

jsonLegacy.power: I knew you'd turn on me, so I poisoned your snacks three weeks ago.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p3 BL

cards.power: You MUST betray an ally this turn. If you have no ally, betray yourself (discard 2 cards).
cards.lore: It's a compulsion. Like sneezing, but with more knives.
cards.gradeReason: 'Like sneezing, but with knives.' You are now this porcupine. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: apologetic porcupine surrounded by startled animals with quills in their backs. Mood: compulsive remorse.

jsonLegacy.power: It's a compulsion. Like sneezing, but with knives.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p3 BR

cards.power: Challenge the current leader. If you lose, apologize profusely and draw 1 card.
cards.lore: Standard operating procedure: Grovel to the face, plot against the back.
cards.gradeReason: Transformers archetype, universal office archetype, win-win framing. Every table has a Starscream.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: ambitious eagle in subordinate uniform plotting with a crown visible in its eyes. Mood: barely concealed ambition.

jsonLegacy.power: Challenge the current leader. If you win, congratulations. If you lose, congratulations.
jsonLegacy.lore: Standard operating procedure for number twos everywhere.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p4 TL

cards.power: Copy the action of the player to your right. Do it worse.
cards.lore: I agree with whatever you just said, sir, especially the part that contradicts what you said yesterday.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic is clear and the submission is legible, but the dog art does more work than the text.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: eager spaniel in a suit nodding violently at a briefcase-holding figure. Mood: performative agreement.

jsonLegacy.power: Copy the action of the player to your right.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p4 TR

cards.power: Take a card someone else just played. Put it in your score pile. It's yours now.
cards.lore: I made this. (I did not make this).
cards.gradeReason: 'Put it in your hand and announce: I made this.' This is improv gold. Live it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: magpie presenting someone else's nest as its own to impressed birds. Mood: brazen theft with good PR.

jsonLegacy.power: Take a card from the top of the pile. Put it in your hand and announce: 'I made this.'
jsonLegacy.lore: I made this.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p4 BL

cards.power: If a player is eliminated, take their seat and their hand.
cards.lore: Break a leg. Seriously. I have a crowbar.
cards.gradeReason: Theatre-revenge concept lands, but the crowbar punchline needs an audience who gets it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: nervous toad in understudy costume holding a crowbar behind a curtain. Mood: theatrical menace.

jsonLegacy.power: Break a leg. Seriously. Have a crowbar.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p4 BR

cards.power: Overthrow the player with the most points. Swap point totals with them.
cards.lore: Look at me. I am the Captain now. Until the Lemurs get hungry.
cards.gradeReason: 'Look at me — I am the leader now.' That's not a card. That's a personality transplant in one sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: lion in torn suit standing on a toppled throne with a crown slightly too large. Mood: triumphant chaos.

jsonLegacy.power: Overthrow the player with the most points. Look at me — I am the leader now.
jsonLegacy.lore: Look at me. I am the leader now. Let's get hungry.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p5 TL

cards.power: Force another player to make a move of your choice.
cards.lore: Dance, little fly. The web was never about catching you; it was about employment.
cards.gradeReason: You literally make another player your puppet. The spider art + 'dance little fly' seals it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: enormous spider controlling a tiny figure on strings above a card table. Mood: elegant villainy.

jsonLegacy.power: Force another player to make a move on your behalf. Dance, little fly. The web is more robust than you think.
jsonLegacy.lore: Dance, little fly. The web is more robust than you think.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p5 TR

cards.power: Break an alliance. Take all shared resources. Lose 1 turn because you are now lonely.
cards.lore: The partnership is dissolved. Also, you are dissolved.
cards.gradeReason: 'Also, you are dissolved.' That second sentence is why this is Grade 1 and not just a break-up card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: cobra with a gavel dissolving two signatures on a parchment. Mood: corporate dissolution.

jsonLegacy.power: The partnership is dissolved. Also, you are dissolved.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p5 BL

cards.power: Call a meeting. Everyone gives you 1 card. If they refuse, they lose 1 life.
cards.lore: This meeting could have been an email, but then I wouldn't get to eat you.
cards.gradeReason: Office-humour punchline is fine but the betrayal angle is underdeveloped. Weakest crab in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: crabs in business attire around a tiny conference table, one eyeing the exit desperately. Mood: corporate ennui.

jsonLegacy.power: This meeting could have been an email but also wouldn't get to be alone with you.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p5 BR

cards.power: Peek at everyone's hand. Reveal one card to the group.
cards.lore: I'm not digging for worms. I'm digging for dirt.
cards.gradeReason: 'I'm not digging for worms. I'm digging for dirt.' You become the mole. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: mole in a hard hat surrounded by stacks of stolen dossiers underground. Mood: gleeful surveillance.

jsonLegacy.power: Peek at everyone's hands. Nobody needs to know for another three rounds.
jsonLegacy.lore: I'm not digging for worms. I'm digging for dirt.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p6 TL

cards.power: Play a card on someone else's turn. It counts as their move, but you choose the target.
cards.lore: I'm on your side. And his side. Mostly my side.
cards.gradeReason: The 'you've already switched sides' reveal is a performance instruction. Table immediately understands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: fox wearing two ties, one for each team, showing different cards to different players. Mood: cheerful duplicity.

jsonLegacy.power: Play a card that makes someone else win. The bet is: you've already switched sides.
jsonLegacy.lore: Pick a side. And then pick a different one.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p6 TR

cards.power: Name a card. If an opponent has it, they must discard it.
cards.lore: I sing like a bird. Specifically, a bird who wants a plea deal.
cards.gradeReason: Funny line but it's a quip without a game action. What do you actually do at the table?
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: nervous pigeon in witness-protection sunglasses speaking into a police microphone. Mood: reluctant confession.

jsonLegacy.power: I sing like a bird. Specifically, a bird who wants a plea deal.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p6 BL

cards.power: Retrieve a card from the discard pile (the graveyard). Play it immediately.
cards.lore: Reports of my death were greatly exaggerated to collect the insurance money.
cards.gradeReason: Mark Twain reference is nice but the insurance-fraud mechanic needs more performative scaffolding.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: skeleton in a suit presenting a forged death certificate to a stunned insurance agent. Mood: administrative fraud.

jsonLegacy.power: Reports of my death were somewhat exaggerated — to collect the insurance money.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p6 BR

cards.power: Give one of your bad cards to a player with more points (your "parent").
cards.lore: Thanks for the food, Mom. Now get out of my room/nest/kingdom.
cards.gradeReason: Domestic betrayal with a Shakespearean lore kicker. Works for parents in the room.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: young bird leaving a nest with a tiny suitcase, parent birds watching in shock. Mood: ungrateful departure.

jsonLegacy.power: Give one of your best cards to a player with more than two kids.
jsonLegacy.lore: Thanks for the food. Goodbye, home. I'm off to ruin my new kingdom.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p7 TL

cards.power: Sacrifice a lower-value card to save a higher-value card.
cards.lore: I brought you into this world, and I can take you out for a snack.
cards.gradeReason: Every player who has a parent gets this. Delivery depends on the player who holds it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: disappointed hamster parent holding up a report card with a red F to a cowering offspring. Mood: parental disappointment.

jsonLegacy.power: Hand the 'I would have been a better card' to a player with fewer cards.
jsonLegacy.lore: I thought you liked this level. Now I'm going to tell you what I really think.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p7 TR

cards.power: Reveal a secret. Force a player to swap their hand with the deck.
cards.lore: He has your eyes. But he has the milkman's beak.
cards.gradeReason: Milkman gag lands reliably. Not a deep mechanic but the reveal energy is present.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: proud swan father presenting a very different-looking cygnet to confused relatives. Mood: awkward revelation.

jsonLegacy.power: He had your eyes. But he has the milkman's book.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p7 BL

cards.power: Eliminate a player who belongs to the same 'faction' or 'suit' as you.
cards.lore: It's a special kind of evil. The kind that saves on holiday gifts.
cards.gradeReason: GoT resonance works, mechanic is clean, but 'force them to forfeit gifts' is slightly passive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: praying mantis in medieval armour raising a blade against a nearly identical praying mantis. Mood: fratricidal sorrow.

jsonLegacy.power: Force the player who betrays you first to forfeit their gifts.
jsonLegacy.lore: It's a special kind of awful.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p7 BR

cards.power: If an opponent helps you, steal half their points next turn.
cards.lore: Surprise! I was working for the Empire/Corporation/Ex-Boyfriend all along!
cards.gradeReason: Spy-romance trope is legible but the 'ex-boyfriend' kicker needs improv chops to land fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: glamorous black widow spider removing a tiny spy disguise to reveal an enemy badge. Mood: romantic espionage reveal.

jsonLegacy.power: Surprise! I was working for the enemy. I hope your ex-boyfriend is OK.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p8 TL

cards.power: Force a player to attack you. Reflect the damage back to them.
cards.lore: It's not love. It's bioluminescent predatory bait. Easy mistake.
cards.gradeReason: 'A clipboard' at the end saves this. The mechanics are explained but the vibe is present.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: deep-sea anglerfish with a glowing heart-shaped lure and a hidden clipboard. Mood: clinical seduction.

jsonLegacy.power: It's not love. It's entrapment, predatory mating rituals and a clipboard.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p8 TR

cards.power: Abandon an ally during a challenge. You gain 2 points; they lose 2.
cards.lore: I'm with you until the end. Or until it gets slightly inconvenient.
cards.gradeReason: Describes the archetype cleanly but asks nothing of the player. Wave goodbye and sit down.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: penguin in a team scarf walking away as their team loses on a scoreboard. Mood: cheerful abandonment.

jsonLegacy.power: I'm with you! Unless you're losing. Good luck, sir.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p8 BL

cards.power: Play a card that looks like an attack but actually heals someone.
cards.lore: I was trying to save you! Why are you hitting me with a newspaper?
cards.gradeReason: The misunderstanding-as-betrayal angle is fresh. Newspaper detail is gold. Needs table energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: good-natured dog being swatted with a newspaper while holding a just-rescued kitten. Mood: unjust punishment.

jsonLegacy.power: Was trying to save you! Why are you hitting me with a newspaper?

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p8 BR

cards.power: Switch from "Good" to "Evil." All your healing cards become damage cards.
cards.lore: Being a good boy was boring. I want to chew the furniture.
cards.gradeReason: Wrestling's most dramatic moment, built into a mechanic. Every table has a Face who's ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: golden retriever removing a hero cape to reveal a villain costume underneath, grinning. Mood: liberating corruption.

jsonLegacy.power: Switch from 'Good' to 'Evil': All your Healing cards become damage cards.
jsonLegacy.lore: Being a good boy was boring.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p9 TL

cards.power: Switch from 'Evil' to 'Good': All your Damage cards become healing cards.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect pair to Face-Heel. The redemption arc in a single card flip. Standing ovation energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: growling wolf mid-transformation, fur softening, holding out a flower instead of fangs. Mood: reluctant redemption.

cards.power: Adopt the special ability of the player to your left.
cards.lore: I find their culture superior. Also, the shrimp is better here.
cards.gradeReason: Interesting defection concept but 'adopt the customs' is vague enough to stall a table cold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: pink flamingo wearing another bird species' plumage, blending awkwardly into a flock. Mood: enthusiastic assimilation.

jsonLegacy.power: Adopt the customs and identity of the player to your left.
jsonLegacy.lore: I find their culture superior. Also, the offering is better here.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p9 BL

cards.power: Help an opponent win a challenge against your own team.
cards.lore: I welcome our new insect-eating overlords.
cards.gradeReason: Collaboration-as-betrayal is clear. The Simpsons line seals the historical reference nicely.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: fat pig in a militia uniform shaking hands with the opposing general while his own army watches. Mood: collaborative treason.

jsonLegacy.power: Help an opponent win a challenge against your own team.
jsonLegacy.lore: I welcome our new Kayfabizarro overlords.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p9 BR

cards.power: Give a gift card to an opponent. When they flip it, they lose 3 cards.
cards.lore: Beware of Greeks bearing gifts. Also beware of Mice bearing giant wooden Cats.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone knows the horse. Everyone plays the gift anyway. That's the joke. That's the game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: enormous wooden cat on wheels being accepted as a gift, tiny armed mice visible through cracks. Mood: ancient grift.

jsonLegacy.power: Give a gift card to an opponent. When they flip it, it explodes into cards.
jsonLegacy.lore: Beware of Greeks bearing gifts. Also beware of gift-bearing giant wooden Cats.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p10 TL

cards.power: Play a high-value card face down. If someone attacks it, they are eliminated.
cards.lore: It looked delicious. It tasted like a snapped spine.
cards.gradeReason: 'Or do they?' is doing heavy lifting. The mousetrap mechanic lands but needs theatrical delivery.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: enormous mousetrap baited with a glowing trophy card, small paw reaching toward it. Mood: irresistible danger.

jsonLegacy.power: Play a high-value card face down. If someone steals it, they win. Or do they?
jsonLegacy.lore: It looked delicious. It tasted like a snapped spine.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p10 TR

cards.power: Negate an accusation. The accuser must apologize and discard a card.
cards.lore: Who, me? I'm just a lil' guy. You wouldn't hit a lil' guy.
cards.gradeReason: 'I'm just a lil' guy' is a perfect meme anchor. Mechanic is punishing and fun.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: enormous guilty-faced dog doing puppy eyes while surrounded by chewed furniture. Mood: weaponised innocence.

jsonLegacy.power: Claim an accusation. The accuser must apologize and discard a card.
jsonLegacy.lore: Who, me? I'm just a lil' guy. You wouldn't hit a...

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p10 BL

cards.power: Invite all players to roll a die. Lowest roll is executed.
cards.lore: The Red Wedding was a bit much, but the catering was exquisite.
cards.gradeReason: Red Wedding reference will make half the table gasp. Elimination mechanic adds genuine table dread.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: ravens at a wedding banquet suddenly revealing weapons under their formal wear. Mood: festive massacre.

jsonLegacy.power: Call everyone to assemble to your right. The lowest roll is eliminated.
jsonLegacy.lore: The Red Wedding was more fun until the catering was expunged.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p10 BR

cards.power: Select an opponent. Both choose "Snitch" or "Silent." Snitch/Silent = Snitch wins big. Both Snitch = Both lose.
cards.lore: If I talk, I walk. If we both talk, we cook.
cards.gradeReason: Game theory as a live performance. The simultaneous choice moment is the best 10 seconds in this deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: two skunks in police interview rooms choosing cards simultaneously through a glass wall. Mood: agonising game theory.

jsonLegacy.power: Select an opponent. Both choose 'Snitch' or 'Silent' simultaneously. Snitch + Silent = Snitch wins. Both Snitch = Both lose.
jsonLegacy.lore: If I talk, we all die. If we both talk, we cook.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p11 TL

cards.power: Cancel combat. Then, immediately attack for double damage.
cards.lore: White flag? No, that's just a napkin I'm using to wipe the floor with you.
cards.gradeReason: Fake surrender is peak kayfabe. 'That's my tablecloth' is the FrizzleBob line of the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: bear waving a white cloth while winking, cards hidden behind its back, winner's grin visible. Mood: strategic humility.

jsonLegacy.power: Appear to lose. Immediately, you win your biggest lost card back.
jsonLegacy.lore: White flag? No, that's my tablecloth. I'm going to wipe the floor with you.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p11 TR

cards.power: No one can attack anyone until your next turn.
cards.lore: If I move, you shoot. If you shoot, he shoots. Let's just stand here and die of thirst.
cards.gradeReason: Mexican standoff energy is great but the 'die of stress' resolution is anticlimactic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: three meerkats in standoff positions each holding a tiny pistol, all sweating profusely. Mood: escalating mutual dread.

jsonLegacy.power: Standoff situation. No one can make a move until someone acts first. Let's stand here and die of stress.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p11 BL

cards.power: Sacrifice your best card to automatically win the game in 3 turns (unless you die first).
cards.lore: I lost the battle to win the war. And the parking space.
cards.gradeReason: Sacrifice-to-win is pure chess drama. 'And the parking spot' grounds the cosmic in the mundane perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: owl in chess master pose pushing a queen piece toward an opponent with a knowing smile. Mood: calculated sacrifice.

jsonLegacy.power: Sacrifice your best card to a rival to win the game on three previous turns.
jsonLegacy.lore: I lost the battle to win the war. And the parking spot.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p11 BR

cards.power: Sell out an ally for 5 resource tokens.
cards.lore: The price of loyalty is surprisingly affordable in this economy.
cards.gradeReason: Biblical betrayal in four words. 'Surprisingly affordable in this economy' is the twist that makes it G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: rat sliding a bag of coins across a table while pointing at an oblivious friend. Mood: transactional Judas energy.

jsonLegacy.power: Sell an ally for 5 resource tokens.
jsonLegacy.lore: The price of loyalty is surprisingly affordable in this economy.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p12 TL

cards.power: Offer a card to a player. If they accept, they die.
cards.lore: A toast! To your health... or lack thereof.
cards.gradeReason: Classic poisoned gift mechanic. The toast lore is perfect. Needs a player willing to ham the offer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: elegant cobra in formal wear raising a jewelled goblet with a small skull floating inside. Mood: aristocratic menace.

jsonLegacy.power: Offer a card to a player. If they accept, they lose a turn.
jsonLegacy.lore: A toast! To your health... or lack thereof.

textSource.source: PDF v05 Uncle_FrizzleBobs_Kayfabizarro_Kards_TRUST_&_BETRAYAL - ADD web.pdf p12 TR

cards.power: Retroactively cancel a deal you made last turn.
cards.lore: It doesn't count if my digits were intertwined. International law.
cards.gradeReason: The 'international law' kicker is funny but the mechanic is retroactive and hard to police at a real table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink cartoon. Subject: grinning monkey sealing a handshake with one hand, other hand behind back with crossed fingers. Mood: legalistic deception.

verdict: The strongest thematic deck in the corpus. Trust & Betrayal is the Kayfabizarro wheelhouse — every card names an archetype every player has lived. PRISONER'S DILEMMA and I SURRENDER, SUCKERS! alone are worth the price of the soul. Slight sag in the middle section where G3 cards (CANNON FODDER, GOING NATIVE, BURNER PHONE) explain instead of invite. But the deck closes on ET TU, BRUTE? and CURSE YOUR SUDDEN BUT INEVITABLE BETRAYAL — a one-two sucker-punch. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 56 betrayal archetypes from Judas to the Quisling to Starscream. For everyone who's ever been stabbed in the back — and honestly, for everyone who's held the knife.

coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Price: YOUR SOUL + scissors + REDACTED stamp = complete betrayal atmosphere

coverQA.coverNote: Best cover since EPSTEIN DECK. 'Price: YOUR SOUL' combined with the scissors-to-the-rabbit is a genuinely surprising image that earns a double-take. The REDACTED stamp on KayfaBIZARRO is the right level of self-aware. This one goes viral on the title alone.

notes: 14 card pages x 4 cards = 56 cards. PDF is iOS-generated image-only (no extractable text layer). Two fonts in use: Permanent Marker (power text on some cards) and Architects Daughter (lore/power on others) — both baked in as images, causing moderate legibility issues on smaller text at web PDF resolution. FACE-HEEL TURN and HEEL-FACE TURN appear on the same page (p.9) — distinct by stat values and art but could benefit from stronger visual differentiation. Cards 29+30 are a paired mechanic set, unique in this deck. RAF stat boxes confirmed present on all cards (three-value corner system).

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: TRUST & BETRAYAL – Every Stab in the Back, Now a Move You Can Throw (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Judas got thirty pieces of silver and two thousand years of brand recognition. The back-stab has always been the best-paid move in the room.

You file your betrayals under things that were done to you: the friend who leaked the secret, the partner who rewrote the story, the colleague who smiled through the whole meeting and then walked off with the credit. Fair enough. But somewhere in that stack is a card you played yourself, the time you folded first, surrendered early, or broke the oath because keeping it cost too much. This deck hands you both ends of the knife and asks which one you perform tonight.

This is wrestling for the oldest move in human politics. You announce the betrayal, you commit to it out loud, and the table rules whether it lands as tragedy, farce, or a double-cross clean enough to applaud. 56 cut-and-play cards, from the historical to the cartoonish, every one of them a way to turn on someone with style.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Trust & Betrayal Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring PRISONER'S DILEMMA (rat first, rat best), ET TU, BRUTE? (the friend in the front row holding the longest blade), and CURSE YOUR SUDDEN BUT INEVITABLE BETRAYAL! for the heel who was always going to turn and wanted you to know it.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No accounting, no win conditions to memorize, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and a table that decides what holds.
- The Turncoat Engine: the paired Face-Heel Turn and Heel-Face Turn that let any player flip allegiance mid-scene, plus a two-card combo, I SURRENDER, SUCKERS! into THE OATH-BREAKER, built to detonate a fragile alliance at the exact moment it hurts most.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This deck runs with the Komik Kard Kult Klub. Grab it once and you are in the cycle: future expansions and new archetypes in this line land in your library as free updates. The roster of traitors only grows.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
Betrayal is the cheapest thing in the world to suffer and the most expensive to say out loud. I make these so people can play with the knife instead of just flinching from it. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Use it. Play it. Run the double-cross where nobody actually gets hurt. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next batch of cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Trust is a story two people agree to tell. Betrayal is the moment one of them stops narrating and keeps the pen."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
